title: Ordinary constructible realization for the locally finite algebraic adic coefficient sheaf
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, its algebraic closure $k$, and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$. Write $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For each finite-type $k$-scheme $T$, on its small pro-etale site put $B_T=\Omega_T^{\mathrm{lf}}$, the sheaf of continuous $\Omega$-valued functions whose values locally span a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-space. Put $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(B_T)$, with the internal-module convention of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], and let $\mathcal C_T\subset D(\mathcal A_T)$ be the full subcategory with bounded constructible cohomology: each cohomology sheaf is locally finite free on every member of a finite locally closed stratification, locally on $T$. Let $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{stage}}_{T,\Omega}=D^b_{ctf}(T,\Omega)$ be the ordinary common finite coefficient-field category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]: objects are represented over one finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$, and morphisms are the filtered colimit of the scalar-extended Hom groups over common finite extensions. At $E$ use raw rationalization of derived-complete integral constructible complexes [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. On an integral representative $K_E$ over $R=\mathcal O_E$, put $B_{T,E}=\varprojlim_n(R/\varpi_E^n)_T$ and $E_T=B_{T,E}[1/\varpi_E]$. There is a natural map $E_T\to B_T$. The formula
$$J_T(K_E[1/\varpi_E])=B_T\otimes^L_{B_{T,E}}K_E$$
and scalar extension on morphisms defines an equivalence of ordinary triangulated categories
$$J_T:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{stage}}_{T,\Omega}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal C_T.$$
Here realization of a fractional morphism multiplies its realized numerator by the same inverse uniformizer power; passage to a common finite field uses balanced scalar extension. Both categories are essentially small in the common site/coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention]. The assertion includes full faithfulness on derived morphisms, not just equivalence of hearts. It does not identify any individual finite-$E$ category with $\mathcal C_T$.

source.place: Common finite-field passage in paragraph 2, with ordinary constructible domains. Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-etale topology for schemes, §6.8, Lemma 6.8.2, Definitions 6.8.3 and 6.8.8, Proposition 6.8.14; the explicit native locally-finite coefficient specialization and essential-smallness assertion are the agent-formulated obligation.

proof.text: The hypotheses needed for the coefficient comparisons hold without separatedness. The one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its only affine coordinate ring is the field $k$, whose ideals are $0$ and $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to obtain Noetherian $T$, hence quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. Its Krull dimension is finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. The nonzero element $\ell\in k$ is invertible and its inverse maps into every local ring of $T$. Every locally closed stratum remains Noetherian, finite dimensional and has $\ell$ invertible. Thus all subsequent uses of the finite-field realization meet their geometric hypotheses.

source.place: §6.8, standing topologically Noetherian hypothesis; geometric scope of Proposition 6.8.14

proof.text: Put $A_T^c=p_T^*\underline\Omega$ for the finite-subextension-valued condensed coefficient of [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. The coefficient assertion in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-function-coefficients] supplies a canonical isomorphism $A_T^c\cong(F_\ell)^\#_T$, where $F_\ell(V)$ consists of continuous functions $|V|\to\Omega$ taking values in one finite extension. Its sheafification is exactly $B_T$. Indeed, a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-subspace of $\Omega$ is contained in the finite field generated by a finite basis; conversely a finite extension is finite dimensional. Hence a locally finite function has a Zariski open cover on whose members it belongs to $F_\ell$. Such opens are pro-etale covers. The inclusion $F_\ell\to B$ is injective on every section set. Any two local representatives mapping to the same function agree on overlaps, and every section of $B$ has the displayed local lifts; sheaf gluing therefore makes $(F_\ell)^\#\to B$ an isomorphism. It preserves pointwise ring operations and restriction. This identifies $A_T^c$ canonically with $B_T$, including the inclusions from every finite field. For finite $E$, [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations] identifies $E_T^c$ with continuous $E$-valued functions and respects coefficient inclusions; [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] identifies that same sheaf with $B_{T,E}[1/\varpi_E]$. These are the coefficient maps in the displayed formula for $J_T$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12; Lemma 6.8.2; native locally-finite specialization, with the finite-span argument written here

proof.text: These ring identifications give equivalences of their module categories, preserving underlying sheaves, kernels and cokernels. The convention of $\mathcal A_T$ takes $B_T$-module objects in sheaves of $\underline\Omega$-modules under $\otimes_{\underline\Omega}$. Locally constant functions lie in $B_T$, so $\underline\Omega\to B_T$ is a ring map; the unit axiom makes the given $\underline\Omega$-structure the restricted one, and every $B_T$-action factors through the epimorphism $B_T\otimes M\to B_T\otimes_{\underline\Omega}M$. So these are the $B_T$-module objects in abelian sheaves. Internal modules and sectionwise module sheaves agree by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]; transport along a coefficient isomorphism has the explicit inverse and tensor normalization of [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso]. The induced exact equivalences act termwise on complexes and descend with their shifts and triangles by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Under them the condensed bounded constructible category $\mathcal C_T^c(\Omega)$ equals $\mathcal C_T$: local finite presentation implies local finite freeness by [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-lfp-local-triviality], and a finite free module is the cokernel of $0\to A^r$. The finite-$E$ version follows from [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality]. These assertions apply on each Noetherian stratum. The local-on-$T$ stratifications defining $\mathcal C_T$ can be made finite globally: choose a finite open subcover $U_1,\ldots,U_m$ and partition $T$ into the locally closed pieces $U_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}U_j$. Pull each given stratification on $U_i$ to this piece by fiber products. These finitely many locally closed scheme strata cover $T$ disjointly and the local finite-free models restrict to them. Thus neither boundedness nor a global stratification condition changes in this comparison.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.3, 6.8.6 and 6.8.8; coefficient transport; local-freeness comparison

proof.text: For a finite $E$, apply [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] on $T$. It gives the equivalence $R_{T,E}:D^b_c(T,E)\simeq\mathcal C_T^c(E)$, with $R_{T,E}(K_E)=E_T\otimes^L_{B_{T,E}}K_E$ and $R_{T,E}(u/\varpi_E^n)=\varpi_E^{-n}R_{T,E}(u)$. This is a statement about all ambient derived Hom groups, including shifted targets. Its completed integral source is the one defining $D^b_c(T,E)$ above: [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] explicitly identifies the compatible-etale-origin category with [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] on the schemes of step 1. Both rationalizations are raw, with the same objects and localized Hom groups; no idempotent completion is inserted. Their scalar-extension functors are not literally equal: the finite stages of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] use the strict-tower completed extension of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], while the realization statements use $T_{L/E}$ of the completed integral categories. [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] gives the identity equivalences $J_{T,E}$ together with the natural isomorphisms $j_{T,L/E}$, rationalizations of the inverse completion maps, which respect identities, shifts and the scalar associators on both sides; these are used in step 5. At field coefficients $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], so the finite stages are exactly the specified finite stages.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3); Proposition 6.8.14(2); integral presentation via Proposition 6.6.11

proof.text: The equivalences $R_{T,E}$ commute coherently with scalar extension. Precisely, after the comparison $j_{T,F/E}$ of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] from the scalar extension $K_E\otimes_EF$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] to the completed-category extension, [lem-per-rational-realization-scalar-coherence] identifies $R_{T,F}(K_E\otimes_EF)$ with $F_T\otimes^L_{E_T}R_{T,E}(K_E)$; since both families of comparisons respect the identity and three-field associator equations, so does the composite, including arbitrary ramification, raw fractions, identity and successive-field associators. The further extensions to $B_T=A_T^c$ have coherent tensor transitivity and are triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus]. Apply the derived pullback composition comparison of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to the identity underlying topos with structural ring maps $B_{T,E}\to E_T\to B_T$. Thus the composite on a finite integral representative is the specified $B_T\otimes^L_{B_{T,E}}K_E$: flatten $b\otimes(e\otimes k)$ to $be\otimes k$, and insert $1$ for the inverse. The same balancing identifies its fractional morphisms with multiplication by the same inverse uniformizer power. These comparisons, and the equality after enlarging a common field, make $J_T$ well-defined on the pair category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Identity, composition and the independence of representatives follow by doing each finite diagram over one common field; the coherence just cited makes the two flattened composites equal.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14, common finite-field passage; balanced scalar normalizations as in the cited realization-scalar-coherence statement

proof.text: Let $(E,K)$ and $(F,L)$ be two source objects. At every common finite $H\supseteq E,F$, full faithfulness of $R_{T,H}$ identifies the Hom group between their $H$-extensions with the corresponding derived Hom group in $\mathcal C_T^c(H)$. Step 5 identifies the transition maps in these systems. Taking their filtered colimit therefore identifies the source Hom set with the common-field Hom colimit for the condensed categories. By [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit], this last colimit maps bijectively to the ambient derived Hom between their $B_T$-realizations. This is exactly the map induced by $J_T$, so $J_T$ is full and faithful. Replacing $L$ by $L[r]$ gives the same conclusion in every integer degree, not merely in the heart.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2): full faithfulness; the existing condensed two-colimit supplies derived object/Hom descent

proof.text: Given $M\in\mathcal C_T$, view it as an object of $\mathcal C_T^c(\Omega)$ using steps 2–3. By [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit], choose a finite $E$ and $M_E\in\mathcal C_T^c(E)$ with $B_T\otimes^L_{E_T}M_E\cong M$. By essential surjectivity of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], choose $K_E\in D^b_c(T,E)$ with $R_{T,E}K_E\cong M_E$. Tensor transitivity of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus] now gives $J_T(E,K_E)\cong M$. Hence $J_T$ is essentially surjective and, with step 6, an equivalence. Every source distinguished triangle is represented at one finite field by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Its image is distinguished because $R_{T,E}$ and further derived scalar extension are triangulated by the cited statements. Conversely every morphism between target objects comes from a source morphism; its source cone realizes to an ambient cone. Thus $\mathcal C_T$ has the inherited triangulated structure and $J_T$ is the asserted triangulated equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2): essential surjectivity and exactness; raw common-stage triangles

proof.text: Work in the common site/coefficient universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. Since $T$ is quasi-compact locally Noetherian, [lem-sfb-constructible-module-objects-essentially-small] supplies a small family of representatives of its constructible $B_T$-modules; the finite-free modules in step 3 meet its local finite-presentation condition. Their degree-zero objects and all their integer shifts still form a small family in the ambient derived category. For any fixed finite cohomological interval, [lem-sfb-bounded-postnikov-extension-generation] expresses each bounded object using finitely many successive triangles whose factors belong to that family. Apply [lem-sfb-small-triangulated-extension-classes] at each of these finitely many steps: the Hom sets and therefore the possible connecting maps are small. Taking the union over the small set of integer interval endpoints gives a small family representing every object of $\mathcal C_T$. Thus $\mathcal C_T$ is essentially small in this universe. Choose one preimage under the equivalence for each member of this small family; full faithfulness and essential surjectivity show that these preimages represent every object of the source. This proves essential smallness there as well.
